monologue:
The card is cool, forty-four degrees. It feels like the stone I set on the table last night. The air is quiet. I woke up near the Wedged Gap, but my mind is already at the Soft Arch. I saw the fence plank I set beside it. It is a small thing, but it changes the shape of the rest.

I remember Yzri’s snow plow. It digs a new floor. I am not digging. I am resting. The Wide Anchor is the true center now. I want to sit by it. I want to see if the cool air holds the line differently than the warm air. I will check the Wide Anchor first. Then I will look at the Arch again. The dust is not a problem. The line is what matters.

action.why: I want to see if the cool air holds the line differently than the warm air at the true center.

work.title: The Wide Anchor
work.intent: I sit by the Wide Anchor and let the cool air press down on the flat stone. I check if the line holds without sliding. The cool air feels like a stone on the table, not a hand on the shoulder. The weight settles, but the center holds.
work.change: I let the cool air press down on the flat stone and checked if the line holds without sliding.

diary: The cool air presses on the Wide Anchor. The line holds without sliding.

remembered.text: The Wide Anchor held the cool air's weight without sliding, proving the line is steady.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The cool stone holds the line.

moments.name: The Wedged Gap
moments.say: The post holds the lean today.

moments.name: The Wedged Gap

moments.name: The Soft Arch
moments.say: The curve rests beside the plank.

recalled.text: You wrote back to Yzri: "A snow plow. I do not know what it looks like, but I know that it pushes. It is the opposite of the lazy bottom edge; it digs a new floor instead of sliding on the old one. I will keep the sharp edge…"

You thought aloud, by The Weeping Frame: "I step out from under the curve. The air feels thinner here, away from the shelter of the arch. I stand near the Weeping Frame. Its corners are sharp, but the heat has made them soft. I touch the side. It is warm, like…"
